To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adolescents who play more video games and play more violent games are more likely to be hostile, get in more fights, argue with their teachers, and get worse grades in school.

adolescents who play more video games and who play more violent video games have more aggressive cognitions, report more aggressive behaviors, and perform more poorly in school than do adolescents who play fewer video games or who play fewer violent video games.
violent video game exposure is associated with more frequent arguments with teachers and with poorer school performance, in part, because it is associated with higher levels of hostility.

how video game exposure influences the development of aggressive behavior.
the impact of violent video games on the development of aggressive behavior.
the effects of violent video games on adolescent hostility, school performance and aggressive behaviors.

violent video game habits are associated with a number of negative outcomes for adolescents.
violent video games are associated with aggressive behaviors and poor school performance.
violent video games are associated with increased aggression, hostility, and poorer academic performance in adolescents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amount of time spent playing violent video games is related to aggressive cognitions (e.g., hostility) and behaviors (e.g., physical fighting).
the effects of violent video games on adolescents are mediated by the effects of violent games on hostility.
